<objective>
Stand up the Walking Skeleton: the thinnest production-quality end-to-end slice that proves the whole Cena stack and the core tenant-isolation boundary. An owner signs up (with consent), creates a venue through the real anon-key write path, and reads it back on a dashboard through RLS; a second owner is proven unable to read it — via a client-SDK integration test against a local Supabase stack.

**User story (MVP):** **As a** restaurant owner, **I want to** sign up and create my first venue entirely by myself, **so that** I have a private, isolated home for my restaurant's data that no other venue can reach.

Purpose: Every later phase writes on top of this scaffold, this schema, and this RLS boundary. Getting `accounts → venues → venue_members` + `private.get_venue_role()` + the `create_venue` bootstrap RPC right here is the single most expensive thing to retrofit (D-22, one-way).
Output: Next.js + Supabase + shadcn scaffold, migration 0001 (core tenancy + bootstrap RPC + RLS), owner signup→venue→dashboard slice, Vitest client-SDK harness, and the first isolation + consent tests — all green against a local `supabase start` stack.

Requirements covered: ACCT-01, ACCT-02, ACCT-03, ACCT-08.
</objective>

<assumption_delta_decision>
Trigger: pluralization (one owner → multiple venues per ACCT-03; one venue → multiple members per D-22).
Primary noun (generalized identity): the membership graph `accounts → venues (1:N)` and `venues → venue_members (1:N)`.
Decision: **promote** — the multi-venue, multi-member representation is the primary model from migration 0001, not a special case bolted onto a single-venue assumption. Research Pattern 1 already treats `venue_members` as canonical; ACCT-03 and multi-member roles are first-class here (schema full, UI minimal per D-15).
Accepted debt: none (promote, not add-alongside).
Suggested invariant test: sign in as owner A with two venues → sees both; sign in as owner B → sees neither (encoded in tests/rls/venue-isolation.test.ts).
</assumption_delta_decision>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Browser → Server Action | Owner-supplied signup/venue form input crosses into privileged mutations |
| Client → PostgREST (anon key) | Any authenticated user can issue direct table queries + RPC calls; RLS + in-RPC authority are the only gates |
| App code → secret key | `admin.ts` holds the secret key; a leak is a full RLS bypass |
| npm registry → build | Third-party packages enter the trust base at install time |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01-01 | Information Disclosure | venues / venue_members RLS | high | mitigate | Dual venue+role policies via `private.get_venue_role()` enabled in migration 0001 (D-22/D-23); cross-owner denial proven by tests/rls/venue-isolation.test.ts; member-read-own on venue_members prevents owner-user_id enumeration |
| T-01-02 | Information Disclosure / Elevation | `lib/supabase/admin.ts` secret key | high | mitigate | `import 'server-only'` guard; no NEXT_PUBLIC_ secret var (D-24); tests use an inline service-role client, never the guarded module; acceptance grep asserts absence |
| T-01-03 | Elevation of Privilege | create_venue / ensure_account RPCs | high | mitigate | Both SECURITY DEFINER RPCs re-check `(select auth.uid())` (and account ownership) internally; EXECUTE revoked from anon, granted to authenticated only (phase root-cause rule) |
| T-01-04 | Tampering | createVenue Server Action input | medium | mitigate | Zod validation (trimmed non-empty name, currency enum, default∈enabled) + DB CHECK constraints (currency, non-empty enabled_languages, default∈enabled) |
| T-01-05 | Spoofing | Owner session identity | medium | mitigate | middleware uses `getUser()` (revalidates JWT against Auth server), never `getSession()` |
| T-01-06 | Repudiation | Terms & Privacy consent | low | mitigate | terms_accepted_version + terms_accepted_at recorded by ensure_account at account creation (D-21); single-column overwrite on re-acceptance is accepted v1 debt (no consent history) |
| T-01-SC | Tampering | npm installs (next, react, supabase, ssr, vitest, typescript) | high | mitigate | Package Legitimacy Audit in RESEARCH.md + Task 1 blocking-human checkpoint before first install; all [SUS] are `too-new` false positives, no [SLOP] |
</threat_model>
